items.title: Apple’s new study looks to improve the effectiveness of AI health tools
items.summary:
Apple announced a new study today with the goal of better understanding how people interact with conversational AI health tools and how useful their responses actually are. The company is conducting the Apple Health AI Usage Study in collaboration with OpenEvidence, a clinical AI platform used by healthcare professionals that generates answers based on medical information from sources like The New England Journal of Medicine. Participants will use a new iOS app to ask medical questions and then rate the responses based on criteria including accuracy, detail, and relevance.
The app is now available for download, and enrollment starts today,  …

items.title: Vulcan rocket fails, destroying 40 Amazon Leo satellites
items.summary:
ULA Vulcan rocket lifts off on November 15, 2026, carrying 40 Amazon Leo broadband satellites. | Photo: Manuel Mazzanti / NurPhoto via Getty Images	

United Launch Alliance (ULA) suffered what is reportedly its first mission failure in its 20-year history, failing to deliver 40 Amazon Leo satellites to orbit. Leo is Amazon's competitor to SpaceX's Starlink, but it has struggled to get off the ground so far, putting only a small portion of the necessary satellites to challenge Starlink into orbit. Today's launch was supposed to be the first of 38 flights Amazon purchased from ULA.

Fanttik’s S1 Pro electric screwdriver is $40 off in the run-up to Black Friday
items.summary:
Amazon’s early Black Friday promos are already underway, and we’ll be highlighting some of our favorites over the next few days on our Shopping page. Among them is the Fanttik S1 Pro Cordless Electric Screwdriver, which is currently matching its all-time low of $39.99 ($40 off) at Amazon for a limited time.
Fanttik S1 Pro Cordless Electric Screwdriver

Where to Buy:

 $79.99 $39.99 at Amazon
 $79.99 $45.99 at Fanttik 

Fanttik’s rechargeable tool is designed to make everyday household repairs and DIY projects easier, and it does a good job. Verge commerce editor Brandon Widder once called it his go-to electric screwdriver, noting he’s used it to assemble a bed, tighten bike seats, and perform other small- to medium-sized tasks around the house. It offers three adjustable torque settings, so you can use a gentler setting for more delicate jobs like electronics and more power for tougher projects. 
Beyond being a capable electric screwdriver, the Fanttik also comes equipped with a few extra conveniences. For example, it features a built-in LED light to help you see screws in darker spaces, such as under a desk or inside a cabinet. The screwdriver also comes with 16 S2 hardened steel bits, including flathead and Torx bits, all of which fit inside an included magnetic storage case. The rechargeable 2,000mAh battery should handle up to 340 screws on a single charge, too, and it supports USB-C so you can quickly charge it between projects.

LG’s budget-friendly B6E OLED TV is up to 50 percent off this weekend
items.summary:
LG’s B6E was already one of the most affordable OLED TVs you could buy, but it’s an even better deal now that it’s included as part of Best Buy’s latest doorbuster event. Now through the end of today, November 15th, the 55-inch model is 50 percent off, dropping it to an all-time low of $699.99 ($700 off) at Best Buy. If you want a larger 4K set, the 65- and 77-inch models are also discounted, dropping them to $999.99 ($900 off) and $1,499.99 ($1,200 off), respectively.
LG B6E OLED TV

Where to Buy:

 $1399.99 $699.99 at Best Buy (55-inch)
 $1899.99 $999.99 at Best Buy (65-inch)
 $2699.99 $1499.99 at Best Buy (77-inch)

Although it’s not as bright as LG’s pricier C6, the B6E still delivers the excellent contrast and deep blacks OLEDs are often praised for. It’s nearly identical to the standard B6, except it comes with a simpler remote that lacks the motion controls and voice features found on LG’s Magic Remote. It supports Dolby Vision and HDR10 for more lifelike colors and detail in bright and dark scenes, along with Dolby Atmos for more immersive audio. And with Apple AirPlay and Google Cast built in, you can easily stream content from your phone or tablet and access a variety of streaming apps, including Netflix, HBO Max, and YouTube via LG’s webOS platform.
The B6 also offers a lot of features gamers will appreciate. It has a 120Hz refresh rate for modern gaming consoles, which is still plenty fast even if it doesn’t rival the 165Hz refresh rate on the C6. It also offers variable refresh rate support — including Nvidia G-Sync and AMD FreeSync Premium — to help minimize screen tearing. You also get a zippy Alpha 8 Gen 3 AI processor and four HDMI 2.1 ports, making it easy to connect multiple consoles. It may lack some of the more advanced features found on LG’s more premium OLED TVs, but at 50 percent off, the B6 is a great option if you want the benefits of OLED without spending a fortune.

items.title: The Sony Aibo was a robot revolution dressed like a dog
items.summary:
In the 1990s, Sony was absolutely convinced that we were on the precipice of a robot takeover. Pretty soon, the company decided, we'd all be living among countless humanoid robots. Some would be our coworkers; others would be our friends; and at least one would be our pet. And "pet" was exactly what Sony was going for when it created the Aibo. It was supposed to be part of the family.
